_readme: Known-red baseline for scripts/prepush_test_gate.py.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: on 2026-07-26 a red deterministic gate shipped anyway,
waved through as 'pre-existing failures untouched'. 'Pre-existing' was an
unbounded, unowned, unrecorded free pass. This file makes it bounded, owned,
recorded, and expiring.
CONTRACT:
- A test that fails and is NOT listed here BLOCKS the push. No exceptions.
- A test listed here and not yet expired WARNS, naming owner + days left.
- ANY entry past its 'expires' date BLOCKS every push until it is removed
or explicitly re-dated with a fresh reason. An expiry you can ignore is
not an expiry.
- A listed test that now PASSES is reported as a stale suppression; delete
the entry.
- A missing, malformed, or schema-violating file BLOCKS. A suppression list
you cannot read is not a suppression list.
EVERY entry REQUIRES all four fields: test, reason, owner, expires.
'test' is a pytest node id (path::Class::test) or, for coarse short-lived
suppression, a bare test-file path. File-scoped entries suppress the whole
file — use them only when the specific id is unstable, and keep the expiry
days away, not weeks.
'expires' is YYYY-MM-DD (UTC date). Past that date the gate blocks.

entries.reason: self_mod_verify shells out to pytest with --timeout; the resolved interpreter has no pytest-timeout, so the child exits 4 (usage error) and every verdict assertion sees verdict=error/'Timeout'. Env/dependency defect, not a logic defect.
Same root cause: child pytest exits 4 on the unrecognized --timeout flag, so verdict=error instead of pass.
Same root cause: no summary line is produced, so failed_tests comes back empty.
Same root cause: exit 2 (error) instead of the expected exit 1 (fail).
Same root cause: exit 2 (error) instead of the expected exit 1.
Same root cause: full-scope run reports verdict=error/'Timeout' instead of pass.

Self-referential: this test runs the REAL default gate set against this checkout, so it is red whenever ANY other deterministic gate is red. It goes green on its own once the other baseline entries are fixed.
Same self-referential cause: it asserts on the real gate result set, which currently short-circuits on the first failing gate.

One assertion in this file is red at HEAD and is being fixed concurrently by the surface-policy chunk (C5) of the same build. File-scoped because the failing node id moves as C5 rewrites the invariant. NEAR-TERM expiry on purpose: if C5 has not landed by then, this must block rather than linger.

One backend-selection assertion is red at HEAD and env-dependent (passes/skips when mlx_embeddings is absent or the embed daemon is running), so the failing node id is not stable across machines. File-scoped for that reason.
